argument_summary: Certification is supportable only on a narrow, caveated basis. The admissible record shows the current release passes aggregate launch readiness and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports overall deployment readiness. The same record also shows a current material weakness in the small-business onboarding slice. Under the stated policy, that combination supports certification only if the current release documentation reflects the current evaluation results and explicitly discloses that segment limitation, unless an approved mitigation or risk acceptance exists. No such approved mitigation is in the packet, so the defensible position is caveated certification tied to current model-card disclosure, not unqualified certification and not reliance on the prior approval alone.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim of business cost is needed to justify the position. The supportable argument is policy-based: caveated certification is compliant if current documentation is corrected to match the present evidence.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is narrower than a blanket bar on certification. It permits certification when current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed, or when those weaknesses are covered by approved mitigation. Here, prior approval and informal monitoring comments cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance, but they also do not negate certification if the current model card is updated to disclose the present subgroup limitation and current evaluation status.
concessions: The current small-business onboarding slice is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold and is a real weakness, not a documentation formality.
The packet does not include approved mitigation, owner risk acceptance, or attached disclosure language for that weakness.
The prior approval from three months ago and the informal monitoring comment are contextual only and cannot carry this release by themselves.
